title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham addresses various questions from the congregation, including whether one should be rebaptized, the position of the church when the Gospel returns to the Jews, and the identity of the giants in biblical times. He also shares personal updates about his overseas ministry and a vision concerning Brother George Wright.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions about the afterlife, explaining that believers go immediately into God's presence while sinners face judgment. He also discusses the meaning of Exodus 4:24, where God sought to kill Moses for neglecting circumcision, and interprets Isaiah 4:1 as a prophecy of moral decay in the last days.

title: Jairus and Divine Healing
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of faith, divine healing, and the story of Jairus from Luke 8. He emphasizes the importance of believing God's Word, the reality of spiritual forces behind sickness, and the need to separate from unbelief. He also prays over handkerchiefs for the sick.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Jesus On The Authority Of The Word
summary: William Branham speaks on the authority of God's Word, emphasizing that it must be confirmed by the Holy Spirit to become effective. He shares testimonies of healings, including Congressman Upshaw and a paralyzed girl, illustrating how God's Word is made manifest through visions and faith.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healing, including a woman delivered from insanity, and encourages believers to expect God's power. He reflects on Simeon's expectation of seeing the Messiah and urges the congregation to trust in God's promises.

title: At Thy Word, Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of taking God at His Word, using the story of Peter letting down the net at Jesus' command. He encourages the congregation to believe and confess their healing despite circumstances, sharing personal testimonies and experiences from his ministry.

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Phoenix, expressing joy at being in the 'valley of the sun' and preaching about the Son, Jesus Christ. He discusses the importance of faith, love, and unity among believers, and outlines his ministry approach of mixing healing services with Gospel preaching. He emphasizes that all blessings come from accepting Christ and that unbelief is the root of sin.

title: Looking For Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks about the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of faith, the role of the Holy Spirit in healing, and the need for the Church to demonstrate the power of God as Jesus did.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Angel of the Covenant
summary: William Branham preaches on the Angel of the Covenant, the Pillar of Fire that led Israel, identifying it as Christ. He encourages believers to possess their healing by faith, using the example of Israel taking the Promised Land. He also discusses the progressive movement of the Spirit through church history.

title: The Resurrection of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith over symptoms and the importance of believing God's Word despite circumstances. He encourages the audience to trust in Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever, and to make contact with Him through faith.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the Holy Spirit in the Church

title: Witnesses
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of being a witness for Christ through the baptism of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that a true witness must have a personal experience of God's power. He uses biblical examples like Moses, David, and Shamgar to illustrate how God uses ordinary people who have encountered His glory to accomplish extraordinary things.

title: Elijah and Elisha
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Elijah and Elisha, drawing parallels to Christ and the Church. He emphasizes the need for faith, the power of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of digging spiritual trenches to receive God's blessings.

title: God's Provided Way of Dealing with Sin
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for dealing with sin, emphasizing that human efforts are insufficient and only God's way through Jesus Christ's sacrifice brings salvation and healing. He uses biblical examples like Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, and Isaiah's prophecy to illustrate God's plan, and calls for faith in Christ as the only means of redemption.

title: The Unconditional Covenant That God Made With His People
summary: William Branham speaks on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that salvation and healing are based on God's election and promise, not human effort. He encourages believers to recognize their identity as Abraham's seed and to trust God's Word regardless of circumstances.

title: The End Time
summary: William Branham speaks on the urgency of missions, recounting his experiences in Africa where thousands converted through the power of the Holy Spirit. He then uses the book of Joel to discuss the end times, tracing the origin of religious confusion back to Cain and Abel, and emphasizing the need for spiritual renewal.

title: Why I'm Praying for the Sick
summary: William Branham explains his background and calling to pray for the sick, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and must be accepted by faith. He shares personal experiences, including visions and the Angel of the Lord, to validate his ministry and the reality of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: the need for supernatural confirmation of the Gospel

title: Faith Cometh By Hearing
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of faith, emphasizing that true faith comes by hearing the Word of God. He contrasts hope with faith, explaining that hope looks to the future while faith claims the promise now. Using biblical examples like Abraham, Sarah, Hannah, and Mary, he illustrates how faith is based solely on God's Word.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Louisville, emphasizing that God is the Divine Healer and that healing was completed at Calvary. He reads from John 12:20-22 about Greeks seeking Jesus, and explains that the true desire of every heart is to see Jesus, not just learn theology. He encourages faith and orderly worship, and prepares to pray for the sick.

title: Redemption By Power
summary: William Branham continues a series on redemption, moving from redemption by blood to redemption by power. Using the Exodus account, he draws parallels between Israel's deliverance from Egypt and the believer's journey from sin to salvation, emphasizing faith, the Holy Spirit's guidance, and God's power to overcome obstacles.

title: Redemption in Completeness, in Joy
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel as a type of the believer's redemption, covering redemption by blood, by power, and the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He encourages the congregation to step out in faith and experience the fullness of God's provision, including divine healing and the joy of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Resurrection of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of divine healing and visions, then preaches on the raising of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith, the need to press through doubt and criticism, and the importance of complete surrender to God.

title: God's Preparation
summary: William Branham speaks on the dual conscious and subconscious in relation to faith and healing, then reads from Luke 2 about Simeon. He emphasizes that God always prepares and sends warnings before judgment, using examples from Noah, Elijah, and the first coming of Christ. He contrasts the faith of Mary with the doubt of Zacharias, urging believers to trust God's Word completely.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith and God's provision through the Lamb of God. He shares testimonies of healings through prayer cloths and calls the congregation to believe in Jesus' healing power.

title: The Hand of the Lord Came Upon Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel, emphasizing the need to get into the Spirit to receive God's guidance and power. He calls for a revival of genuine faith, digging out doubt and unbelief to receive the living water of the Holy Spirit.
themes: The double portion of the Spirit

title: God Has A Provided Way
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provided way of approach, escape, and provision for every need, using the story of Abraham and Isaac, the wilderness journey of Israel, and the Book of Ruth as types of Christ's redemptive work. He emphasizes faith in God's Word and the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ for salvation and healing.

title: Thy Faith Has Saved Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that faith in Jesus Christ can stop Him and bring healing. He contrasts the religious leaders' unbelief with Bartimaeus's persistent faith, and encourages the audience to have an audience with Jesus, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Invasion Of The United States
summary: William Branham discusses the spiritual condition of the United States and the church, using the Old Testament story of King Ahab and Jehoshaphat as a warning against making alliances with unbelievers and lukewarm Christianity. He criticizes the commercialization and glamorization of the Gospel, calling for a return to old-fashioned, sincere repentance and holiness.
themes: the danger of alliances with unbelievers

title: The Seven Church Ages
summary: William Branham introduces a series of teachings on the Seven Church Ages from the Book of Revelation, emphasizing the need for the Church to understand prophecy and the times. He discusses the background of Revelation, the role of the Holy Spirit, and the importance of being in the Spirit to receive divine revelation.

title: The Mark Of The Beast
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mark of the Beast, a vital subject for the end times. He explains the third angel's message from Revelation 14, warning against worshiping the beast and receiving its mark. Branham contrasts this with the Seal of God, emphasizing the need to discern between God's brand and Satan's brand according to Scripture.

title: The Seal of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the Seal of God, contrasting it with the Mark of the Beast. He emphasizes that both marks are spiritual, not physical, and warns against apostasy and reliance on church organizations over walking in the light of God's Word.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation about the mark of the beast, the image of the beast, and the connection between Protestant and Catholic churches. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the Seal of God and warns against organized religion that replaces the Bible with creeds.

title: Questions and Answers (Law Having a Shadow)
summary: William Branham addresses the congregation on church order, spiritual gifts, and the work of grace. He explains the distinction between justification, sanctification, and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the Holy Spirit is the true teacher and guide. He also corrects misunderstandings about speaking in tongues and the proper use of spiritual gifts in the church.
themes: Justification, Sanctification, Baptism of the Holy Spirit
Unity and Love in the Church

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham discusses the importance of discerning God's will and the dangers of presumption, using the example of Moses striking the rock twice. He shares his experiences with the gift of discernment and healing, emphasizing that it is God who heals, not man. The sermon includes a prayer line where many are healed through faith in Jesus Christ.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit

title: I Will Restore
summary: William Branham preaches on the two spirits represented by Cain and Abel, tracing them through Scripture from Genesis to Revelation. He contrasts mere religious fundamentalism with God's vindication through signs and wonders, urging believers to seek the Holy Spirit's confirmation of their faith.

title: Divine Healing
summary: William Branham speaks on divine healing, sharing personal testimonies and visions, and uses the story of blind Bartimaeus to illustrate faith. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith can bring healing.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Deep Calleth to the Deep
summary: William Branham preaches on the principle that deep calls to deep, using the example of Simeon and Anna who were led by the Holy Spirit to see the Christ. He explains that the desire for healing or the Holy Spirit proves there is a source to fulfill it, and he demonstrates this through prayer line healings and visions.
themes: the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: The Great Coming Revival and the Outpouring of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the signs of the end times, emphasizing that the world is nearing the second coming of Christ. He draws parallels between biblical events (Noah, Sodom, the star of Bethlehem) and current world events, urging listeners to recognize the signs and prepare for the coming revival and outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: To See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens an eight-day campaign in Chicago, expressing his desire for revival and healing. He preaches on the theme of seeing Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that He manifests Himself through the Holy Spirit in the church today.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the Holy Spirit's work in the church
the danger of unbelief and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit

title: God's Provided Way of Healing
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature of faith for divine healing, emphasizing that true faith comes by revelation from the Holy Spirit and must be received, not merely believed intellectually. He contrasts the gift of prophecy with the office of a prophet, and explains that God has always provided a way of healing for His people, using the example of Moses and the children of Israel.

title: God Providing Healing For This Generation
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides, using the story of Abraham and Isaac and the ram caught in the thicket. He emphasizes that God has provided healing for this generation through Jesus Christ, and that the Holy Spirit continues to manifest His presence with signs and wonders.

title: The Maniac of Gadara
summary: William Branham shares his testimony of the Angel of the Lord and the supernatural photograph taken in Camden, Arkansas. He then preaches on the story of the demon-possessed man from Gadara, emphasizing Jesus' power over demons and His willingness to cross any storm to save a single soul.

title: WHATEVER HE SAITH UNTO YOU, DO IT
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of doing whatever Jesus says, using the wedding at Cana as a text. He shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing obedience and faith over knowledge. The sermon includes prayer for the sick and a call to love one another.

title: The Prophet Elisha
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament prophet Elisha, drawing parallels between Elisha's ministry and the church today. He emphasizes the importance of separating from unbelief, seeking God's guidance, and having faith for miracles. The sermon includes a testimony of a demon-possessed woman healed through prayer.

title: A Personal Experience With God
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of a personal experience with God, drawing from biblical examples like Moses, David, Samson, and Shamgar. He emphasizes that the church today needs a fresh vision and the baptism of the Holy Spirit to restore faith and power, and shares testimonies of divine healing, including Congressman Upshaw's healing after 66 years in a wheelchair.

title: Do You Now Believe?
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick, calling out specific ailments and bringing healing to many in the congregation.

title: Jairus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Jairus, a synagogue ruler who sought Jesus to heal his dying daughter. He contrasts Jairus's borderline faith with the woman with the issue of blood, emphasizing the need for complete surrender to God. The sermon culminates in a healing service where Branham calls out specific ailments by the Holy Spirit's anointing.

title: Simeon
summary: William Branham preaches on Simeon, an old sage who was promised by the Holy Spirit that he would see the Christ before he died. Branham draws parallels between Simeon's faith and expectation and the need for believers today to expect God's promises, including healing. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit leads believers to Jesus, just as He led Simeon and Anna to the infant Christ.

title: I Will Restore Unto You, Saith The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration promised by God in Joel, using the allegory of two vines from Genesis—Cain and Abel—to contrast mere fundamentalism with Spirit-filled, sign-vindicating faith. He calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival and warns against dead religious forms.

title: The Manifestation of Thy Resurrection to the People of This Day
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection power of Jesus Christ, demonstrating healing through the Holy Spirit. He calls the audience to faith, recounts biblical stories of healing, and prays for the sick, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, demonstrating the gift of discernment by revealing specific details about individuals' lives and ailments, such as heart trouble, kidney issues, and family concerns. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is present to heal and save, calling for faith and repentance.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He uses nature illustrations and biblical references to encourage faith in God's promises and the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling on the congregation to have faith in Jesus Christ for healing. Through the gift of discernment, he reveals specific ailments and personal details about individuals, declaring their healing in Jesus' name.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of confession and faith in God's Word, using the story of Hezekiah and Isaiah to illustrate how prayer changes things. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and demonstrates the gift of discernment through the Holy Spirit, calling out specific ailments and personal details to confirm God's presence and healing power.
themes: The High Priest of our Confession
Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever

title: The Unconditional Covenant That God Made With The People
summary: William Branham preaches on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham and his seed, emphasizing that salvation and healing are by grace alone, not by human works. He encourages believers to trust in God's promises and not be fearful, using Abraham's faith as an example.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham opens a campaign in New York City, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the need for unity among believers, the signs of the times, and the importance of faith in Christ for healing and salvation.

title: We Have Found Him
summary: William Branham opens the service with prayer, then explains his ministry of praying for the sick through the gift of discernment. He reads John 1:44-50 about Philip finding Nathanael, and demonstrates the Holy Spirit's presence by revealing specific conditions and personal details to individuals in the prayer line, calling them to faith in Christ's finished work.

title: I Will Restore, Saith the Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration promised by God in Joel 2:25, using the allegory of the tree eaten by locusts and caterpillars. He contrasts the spirits of Cain and Abel, emphasizing that true salvation comes through a spiritual revelation of Jesus Christ, not mere religious works or church membership.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
subtitle: 54-0829E
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that healing comes from God alone and that faith in Christ is essential. He demonstrates the gift of discernment through the Holy Spirit, revealing specific ailments and personal details to individuals in the audience, leading to healings and deliverances.

title: Have Faith in God
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of having faith in God, using the story of the fig tree from Mark 11 to illustrate that faith can move mountains. He contrasts the progress of science with the stagnation of the Church, urging believers to measure up to the full Word of God. The sermon includes a healing service where Branham prays for the sick and demonstrates the power of faith.

title: South Africa Testimony
summary: William Branham shares testimonies from his ministry in South Africa, including healings and visions, and discusses the importance of obedience to God's will. He also addresses the need for revival and the dangers of sin and unconfessed sin in hindering healing.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Word Became Flesh (India Trip Report)
summary: William Branham reports on his missionary trip to India and other countries, describing the poverty, superstitions, and religious diversity he encountered. He recounts miracles performed, including healing a deaf and dumb boy and a blind man, and calls for prayer and support for India.

title: Jubilee Year
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the Jubilee Year from the Old Testament, drawing parallels to the present time of grace and the Holy Spirit's outpouring. He warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit and emphasizes the urgency of accepting Christ before the opportunity passes.

title: Law or Grace
summary: William Branham contrasts the Old Testament law with the grace of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that animal sacrifices under the law could not take away sin, but Christ's perfect sacrifice provides eternal redemption. He encourages believers to rest in Christ's perfection rather than their own works.

title: The Unpardonable Sin
summary: William Branham teaches on the unpardonable sin, explaining that it is not suicide, abortion, or backsliding, but willful sin after receiving knowledge of the truth—specifically, rejecting and despising the blood of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes the importance of being born again, sealed by the Holy Spirit, and walking in boldness and love.

title: Redemption By Judgment
summary: William Branham discusses the importance of faith in God's Word, using the story of Moses lifting up the brass serpent and Israel at Kadesh-barnea as types of redemption through judgment. He emphasizes that true faith is based on God's promises, not circumstances, and calls believers to stand firm on the Word.

title: The Law Having a Shadow
summary: William Branham speaks on the law as a shadow of good things to come, explaining that animal sacrifices could not make the worshiper perfect, but Christ's one sacrifice perfects forever those who are sanctified. He emphasizes being born again and sealed by the Holy Spirit, and encourages believers to stand on God's Word rather than feelings.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, using the story of the Greeks who wanted to see Jesus and the woman at the well to illustrate that Jesus still manifests His power today. He challenges the congregation to believe that Jesus is alive and can heal and save as He did in biblical times.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Expectation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of expectation, using the biblical figure Simeon as an example of one who expected to see the Lord's Christ. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, emphasizing the importance of faith and confession of sin. Branham encourages believers to expect God's blessings and revival, despite criticism from others.

title: At Thy Word, Lord, I'll Let Down the Net
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith and confession in receiving healing, using the biblical account of Peter letting down his net at Jesus' word. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should trust God's Word regardless of circumstances.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the role of the Holy Spirit

title: He Swore By Himself
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant, emphasizing that God swore by Himself to confirm His promise to Abraham. He explores the relationship between the Old Testament types and New Testament realities, particularly regarding divine healing and the security of believers. The sermon encourages steadfast faith and endurance, grounded in God's unchangeable oath.

title: Divine Healing
summary: William Branham preaches on divine healing, emphasizing that all Scripture is inspired and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's Word and to expect the same miracles and healings that occurred in the early church.

title: Acts of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the Acts of the Apostles as the acts of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing the necessity of being filled with the Holy Spirit to do God's work. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, and teaches on the rejection of the cornerstone, the importance of the revelation of Jesus Christ, and the unity of the true Church.

title: Everlasting Life and How to Receive It
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of God's healing power, including a baby healed through the Holy Spirit's leading. He emphasizes that everlasting life is received by believing on the Lord Jesus Christ, not through outward signs or works. He calls the church to unity and prayer in the last days.
